newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Top Democrat urges Patten to defend legislature.
newsitem.headline: Top Democrat urges Patten to defend legislature.

text.p: Hong Kong's biggest political party on Wednesday urged Governor Chris Patten to firmly defend the colony's elected legislature and the rule of law, as China prepares to take back the territory from Britain next year.

Democratic Party leader Martin Lee said Patten should not only resist China's plan to scrap the Legislative Council (Legco) and appoint a provisional legislature, he should also outline possible responses to any breach of the handover treaty.
"If he says it's going to be a breach, then I'd like to know what he is going to do about it," Lee said on Hong Kong radio.

Lee, who leads the largest group of elected legislators in Legco, was speaking on a panel with other politicians just hours before Patten's annual policy speeech, the governor's fifth and final "state of the colony" address before the 1997 handover.

"Will the British government, as promised by (Prime Minister) John Major and Malcolm Rifkind, the foreign secretary, take China to the International court of Justice for violation of the Joint Declaration?" Lee challenged.
"Is he going to get his attorney-general to go to the High Court in Hong Kong and ask for an injunction to stop it, which he is entitled to do as a matter of law?" Lee said.

The Joint Declaration is the Sino-British treaty of 1984 that sets out the framework for China to take back Hong Kong from Britain at midnight next June 30, after a century and a half of colonial rule.

China has accused Patten of violating the treaty through reforms that expanded democracy in Hong Kong, and Britain has assailed China's retaliatory plan to abolish Legco, which was elected a year ago for a four-year term.
Lee warned that unless the legislature was rigorously defended, the rule of law in Hong Kong would be dead.

London has publicly opposed China's plan and has said it will use all means to defend the Joint Declaration against violations. But it has stopped short of stating clearly what action it would take if Legco is dissolved.
